text: Settings or a form: each setting takes one value
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: Each factor takes exactly one of its values (FW_Combi(1)) and is crossed with every other factor, so the combinations multiply with each factor added: a pairwise selection usually keeps them few.

text: A workflow: steps whose order matters
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: Steps that may run in any order are a sequence of actions: FW_Combi(k) then FW_Permut() in one row takes k of them in every order (P(n,k)), FW_Permut alone puts all of them in every order (n!).

text: Options that can be switched on together
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: Options on in any mix are a group of any size: FW_Subsets_RANGE(0,n) takes every subset once (2^n).

text: Repeated picks: the same item may come more than once
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: Picks in which an item may repeat are a group with repetition: FW_CombiR(k) then FW_Combi(k) in one row (C(n+k−1,k)); when their order matters too, FW_PermutR(k) then FW_Combi(k) (n^k).

text: Something that may or may not happen
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: An event that may or may not happen is a sudden action (FW_Optional): a test case has it in one of its ways or not at all.

text: None of these: I describe my own factors
hint: Choose this if it is closest to what you test: Start from an empty list: add each thing that varies between test cases as a factor, with its values, then say how one test case uses it.
Replace the factors and rules with the example of the chosen situation, so that you start from a complete scenario and change it to yours.

Move the selected factor up: the test cases' code follows the factors' order.
Move the selected factor down: the test cases' code follows the factors' order.
Each test case takes one value of this factor, like one browser.
Each test case takes the same number of this factor's values, set beside it, like two coupons.

text: Any number of them, within bounds
hint: Each test case takes some of this factor's values, from the fewest to the most set beside it, like any mix of options.

text: No: they form a group, and a+b is the same as b+a
hint: The order of the values does not matter: each group of values is one test case.

text: Yes: they form a sequence, and a+b differs from b+a
hint: The order matters, like steps of a workflow: each order of the values is a test case of its own.

text: A value may appear more than once
hint: Allows a value twice in one test case, like two of the same book in a cart. Only with a fixed number of values.

text: It may or may not happen: a sudden action
hint: Makes the factor a sudden action, like a timeout: test cases are made with it and without it, in every combination with the other sudden actions.
Add the rule the sentence below says to the scenario.
Remove the rule selected in the table.
Every combination becomes a test case: best when they are a few hundred at most.
Keep enough combinations that every value of each factor meets every value of every other factor at least once.
Keep enough combinations that every three values of any three factors meet at least once: more test cases than pairwise.

text: The strongest covering within a number of rows
hint: The Framework picks the strongest covering whose rows fit the number beside it.

text: Search harder for fewer test cases (set-cover)
hint: Takes, each time, the combination that covers most of what is still missing: usually fewer test cases, a little slower.

text: Run every order of each sequence of actions with each kept combination
hint: Keeps the sequences of actions apart from the selection, which then covers the static parameters only; untick it to let the selection choose orders as it chooses values, for fewer test cases.

text: Run a bootstrap once, first, before all the test cases (FW_RunMeFirstOnce)
hint: Adds the bootstrap: code that runs once per run, before any test case, to prepare what they all share and hand them their arguments.

text: Add a check sheet where your test decides its verdict
hint: Adds the sheet check: the place to call the system you test and say whether it misbehaved. Its verdict code is named CHECK_FAILED.
